analysis.title: BP Plc (BP.L): 3Q strong delivery and cash generation; December CMD is the next catalyst. Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on BP (rating since Apr 23, 2018) after 3Q26. 12m price target raised to 760p from 720p (price 624.3p, upside 21.7%). ADR target raised to $60.00 from $57.00 (price $50.35, upside 19.2%). The raise reflects higher cash flow generation and lower net debt estimates.

3Q26 underlying RC operating profit was $13,443mn, c.10% above company-compiled consensus of $12,230mn. Underlying RC net income was $8,458mn, c.15% above consensus of $7,330mn. Customers & Products, helped by higher realized refining margins, commercial optimization and trading, was the largest contributor at $6,948mn vs $6,300mn consensus.

Gas & Low Carbon Energy RC operating profit was $3,183mn vs $2,860mn consensus (+11%), on higher realizations and much stronger gas marketing and trading. Oil Production & Operations was $3,534mn vs $3,350mn consensus (+5%).

Trading and integrated downstream are the differentiators. Management said trading has added an average of about 4 percentage points of ROACE over the last six years. GS sees trading and downstream optimization as earnings upside during market dislocations.

4Q26 faces sequential headwinds: lower upstream production, lower refining throughput after the Gelsenkirchen sale, seasonally lower customer earnings, about $0.8bn higher cash taxes and $1.0-1.5bn higher capex qoq. Trading is typically softer in 4Q. GS still forecasts about $6.7bn of pre-working-capital FCF in 4Q26, vs a 10-year 4Q average of $2.3bn.

Elevated crude tanker rates (elevated since March per management) could add upside because BP runs owned, chartered and spot vessels. Management did not explicitly guide to a freight-related trading benefit in 4Q.

Balance sheet repair is ahead of schedule. Reported net debt excluding leases and hybrids fell $8.4bn qoq to $13.9bn, already below the previous $14-18bn end-2027 target range. Net debt including leases and hybrids fell to $39.3bn from $48.6bn in 2Q26. Net debt-to-equity fell to 34% from 47%.

GS estimates net debt including hybrids can reach $27.8bn by end-2026 (about 20% ND/CE, in line with the EU Big Oil sector average), assuming disposals, FCF and zero buybacks. That is about a year earlier than previously expected. BP's broader financial obligations measure fell to $44.3bn from $53.6bn and is guided to $33-35bn by year-end.

Management still calls leverage too high and balance-sheet strengthening its number-one priority. Excess cash goes first to the remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities, with a committed dividend and disciplined investment. No immediate return to material buybacks is signaled.

The December 15 Strategy and Outlook Update (Capital Markets Day) is the key catalyst. GS estimates a 2026 payout of 42% of pre-OWC CFO (55% previously) and a 4.1% shareholder-return yield vs about 7.8% for the sector, with no buybacks in its forecasts. Clarity on leverage threshold, timing and size of buybacks could lift estimates.

Cost cuts: $4.0bn of cumulative structural reductions achieved since 2023 ($2.8bn in 2024-25, $1.2bn in 9M26) vs a $6.5-7.5bn target by end-2027. GS benchmarking shows up to $7.8bn of potential savings if SG&A moves to the peer median, but cautions that the comparison may overstate the savings.

Upstream: about 15 discoveries, roughly 10 near existing infrastructure. Bumerangue (Brazil) has potential resources of about 8bn barrels. Appraisal starts after drilling at Tupinambá, with the rig potentially moving by YE26. BP is studying an early production system and full-field development, and management now sees concept select by YE27 as premature.
GS values Bumerangue at roughly $3-5bn EV at $60-70/bbl oil (25% recovery, 10% WACC, 2 FPSOs of 200 kbpd, $10bn capex each), or 2-3% of BP EV.

Valuation: 3.2x 2026E EV/DACF vs 6.3x 20-year average and 4.4x for EU Big Oils. 5.2x 2026E P/E vs 10.7x historical and 7.2x for EU Big Oils. 2026E FCF yield 21.3% in the valuation text (the cover table shows 17.7%) vs 6.5% historical and 15.4% for EU Big Oils.

Estimate changes: EPS up about 14%/18%/18% for 2026/27/28E on commodity and refining margin assumptions. GS 2026E EPS is $1.59 (old $1.40), 2027E $1.09 (old $0.92), 2028E $0.88 (old $0.74). 2026E EBIT is $42.3bn (old $39.9bn).

Guidance: FY26 reported upstream production 2,210-2,250 kboe/d (was 2,180-2,270). 4Q26 production 2,090-2,230 kboe/d vs 2,215 in 3Q. FY26 refining throughput 1,390-1,400 kb/d. Underlying tax rate lowered to 31-34% from 35-40%. Capex unchanged at $13.5-14.0bn. Divestment proceeds about $8bn, including about $6bn from the sale of a 65% stake in Castrol, expected to close imminently.

Disposal progress: Gelsenkirchen refinery sold and Austrian mobility and convenience business sold. The UK North Sea sale is described as competitive with offers on the table. Lightsource bp is slower because it is hard to find a buyer for the whole business. Management is prioritizing value over speed.
3Q26 DPS was 8.66 cents, flat qoq and up 4% yoy, in line with GS.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated after a 10% operating profit beat, with the ADR target raised to $60 from $57. Drivers are faster deleveraging, trading and downstream strength, and the December 15 capital return framework.

sector_views.rationale: The report does not state a sector stance. BP trades at a discount to EU Big Oils on EV/DACF (3.2x vs 4.4x), P/E (5.2x vs 7.2x) and FCF yield (21.3% vs 15.4%), and offers a lower shareholder-return yield (4.1% vs about 7.8%).

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported 10/30/2026: underlying RC operating profit $13,443mn vs company-compiled consensus $12,230mn (about +10%). Underlying RC net income $8,458mn vs consensus $7,330mn (about +15%). GS had estimated operating profit of $12,250mn.

3Q26 proforma clean EPS reported at $0.55 vs GS estimate $0.49 and $0.37 in 2Q26. Operating cash flow pre-working capital was $14.3bn vs Visible Alpha consensus $12.9bn. Capex was $3.0bn, in line with the $3.0bn consensus.
3Q26 reported 3Q26 tax rate 28% vs GS estimate 30% and consensus 31%. Dividend 8.66 cents per share, flat qoq, in line with GS.

4Q26 guidance: upstream production 2,090-2,230 kboe/d, refining throughput 1,160-1,210 kb/d vs 1,396 kb/d in 3Q, a significantly lower customers result qoq, and cash taxes about $0.8bn higher qoq. GS 4Q26E EPS is $0.46.
GS estimates (new vs old): 2026E EPS $1.59 vs $1.40, 2027E $1.09 vs $0.92, 2028E $0.88 vs $0.74. The estimate changes are c.+14%/+18%/+18%. GS forecasts no buybacks in its estimates.
risk_factors: Lower oil and gas price realizations than GS expects, especially European gas prices.
Lower-than-expected recovery rates in mature offshore fields, which could mean higher decline rates and lower production growth.
Higher-than-expected costs or capex in future developments.
Materially lower cash returns to shareholders than GS expects, from lower dividends or a change in buyback guidance.
Remaining Gulf of America (Deepwater Horizon) liabilities and slower-than-hoped disposals (Lightsource bp).
charts_described: Exhibit 3 shows BP's 2026 quarterly pre-OWC FCF generation against the 10-year historical average by quarter: 3.5, 3.7, 3.7 and 2.3 for the 10-year 1Q-4Q averages, and 5.6, 8.8, 11.3 and 6.7 for 2026 (4Q26 is GS's forecast).
Exhibit 11 shows the EV sensitivity of Bumerangue: $2,888mn to $7,399mn across oil prices of $60-80/bbl at 25% recovery. At 25% recovery and $65/bbl the value is $4,016mn.
geopolitical: Management cited continued disruption in the Middle East as a drag on 4Q26 upstream production.

tension_points.bull_case: Net debt is already below the 2027 target and cash generation is strong, giving room for buybacks. GS sees greater clarity on the leverage threshold, timing and scale of buybacks at the December 15 update as upside to its zero-buyback estimates.
tension_points.bear_case: Management calls leverage too high and puts the remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities and balance-sheet repair first. It is not signaling material buybacks, and GS's 4.1% shareholder-return yield is among the lowest in the sector.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A December 15 framework with no buyback timetable or leverage threshold would undercut the re-rating case.

tension_points.bull_case: GS forecasts about $6.7bn of pre-OWC FCF in 4Q26, nearly three times the 10-year 4Q average, with upside from elevated tanker rates and the integrated trading model.
tension_points.bear_case: Management guides to lower upstream production, lower refining throughput, a significantly lower customers result, $0.8bn higher cash taxes and $1.0-1.5bn higher capex, with trading typically weaker in 4Q.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rapid balance-sheet repair creates scope for incremental shareholder returns, and clarity on buybacks at the December 15 update could lift estimates.
theme_stances.evidence: greater clarity on the leverage threshold, timing and scale of potential buybacks

theme_stances.key_argument: Integrated trading and refining captured volatility in 3Q and can add upside in periods of dislocation.
theme_stances.evidence: trading has contributed an average ~4 percentage points of ROACE uplift
